subsystems.name: Antenna
subsystems.role: radiates low-frequency radio waves into the ice and receives the weak reflections.

subsystems.name: Transmitter
subsystems.role: generates high-power chirped pulses that penetrate ice with low loss.

subsystems.name: Receiver and digitizer
subsystems.role: captures and digitises faint echoes from internal layers and the base.

subsystems.name: Digital signal processor
subsystems.role: compresses chirps and coherently sums pulses to build a radargram.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: supplies high-voltage pulses and removes heat in vacuum.

subsystems.name: Navigation and attitude
subsystems.role: provides precise orbit and pointing so echoes can be positioned on the surface.

subsystems.name: Data handling
subsystems.role: stores and downlinks the large volume of radar data.

buildSteps.title: Set science requirements
buildSteps.detail: Target depth, layer resolution and ice composition determine the frequency, typically a few MHz for kilometres of penetration up to tens of MHz for shallow layers.

buildSteps.title: Design the antenna
buildSteps.detail: Antenna length scales with wavelength; a spacecraft needs a deployable dipole or array that fits in the launch fairing.

buildSteps.title: Build the transmitter and receiver
buildSteps.detail: A high-power amplifier generates chirped pulses, while a low-noise receiver and a fast switch protect the electronics from the transmit pulse.

buildSteps.title: Implement digital processing
buildSteps.detail: Chirp generation, pulse compression and coherent summing are coded into radiation-tolerant processors.

buildSteps.title: Test on Earth
buildSteps.detail: The sounder is flown over known ice sheets or placed in an anechoic chamber to calibrate timing, gain and polarisation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: The antenna, electronics and power supply are mounted and checked for electromagnetic compatibility with other instruments.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: The antenna is deployed in space and the instrument is switched on to verify operation.

buildSteps.title: Operate and collect
buildSteps.detail: The spacecraft flies repeated ground tracks while the sounder records echoes along each pass.

buildSteps.title: Process the data
buildSteps.detail: Ionospheric distortion is removed, echoes are migrated to true depth, and layers and basal reflections are mapped.

prerequisites.why: penetration requires metres-long wavelengths and high-power pulses that must be switched and received cleanly.
echoes from deep layers are extremely weak and must be integrated over many pulses.
the antenna is far larger than the spacecraft body and must unfold reliably after launch.
converting travel time into depth and detecting liquid water depends on how ice absorbs and bends radio waves.
echo position on the surface depends on knowing where the spacecraft is to within a few tens of metres.

pathway.milestone: orbital sounders map polar ice on Earth and Mars, and have detected buried layers and possible briny water
pathway.unlocks: routine subsurface mapping of ice sheets and polar caps.

pathway.milestone: dedicated sounders on missions to icy moons, such as Europa Clipper and JUICE, probe ice shells and search for subsurface oceans
pathway.unlocks: direct evidence of liquid water beneath the surfaces of ocean worlds.

pathway.milestone: multi-frequency and higher-resolution sounders combined with gravity and magnetic data
pathway.unlocks: confident separation of liquid water from ice and rock.

pathway.milestone: landed or airborne sounders on icy moons, followed by in-situ verification
pathway.unlocks: ground-truth calibration and detailed characterisation of habitable zones.
